summary: Completed backend+frontend verification for ScrapeBadger provider integration. Confirmed masked credential metadata, provider visibility in Integrations UI, deterministic fallback placement, ScrapeBadger request construction via mocks, URL/item-id validation, malformed JSON safety, and provider usage/auth regressions.
action_items: No open functional defects in requested scope after retest.
Consider refactoring backend/server.py (>5k lines) into route modules to reduce regression risk.
MOCKED: ScrapeBadger/eBay/provider network calls were validated only through mocked tests; no live provider calls were made.
critical_code_review_comments: Fixed a real mapping edge case in backend/scraper.py: quantity_available=0 was previously lost by truthy-coalescing, causing incorrect stock mapping.
Adjusted stock_status derivation so zero quantity maps to out_of_stock unless availability explicitly indicates sold/ended.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Used public URL from frontend/.env and admin creds from /app/memory/test_credentials.md (qa@prettycheap.com.au / QaTest123!). Verified ScrapeBadger row exists in Store Management > Integrations > Scraper APIs, with masked saved key metadata and empty credential input value. Backend pytest file now includes extra coverage for eBay AU item-id extraction and invalid JSON handling.
rca of the issue: RCA: ScrapeBadger mapper used `quantity_available or quantity`, so quantity=0 collapsed to fallback None due Python truthiness; this prevented quantity-based sold/out_of_stock detection. Reproduction: parse payload with quantity_available=0 and no explicit availability token. Mitigation applied: preserve zero with explicit None check and derive stock_status using quantity_zero + availability semantics; validated by new targeted tests.
